label: B3 NARROWED: the --pure flag is present in BOTH single-executor if_cli_opencode branches (deep-research-auto.yaml:1619, deep-review-auto.yaml:1547) with identical argv shape, so the research-only framing is falsified; whether the installed OpenCode accepts --pure at all could not be tested because the session dispatch guard refused every opencode invocation including a bare opencode --version, so validity is unproven rather than confirmed.

The research family evaluates branch_on/skip_when and renders dispatchFacts from config.executor.type (8 sites), a key the executor schema does not have - the config declares only kind, and the review family correctly reads config.executor.kind. skip_when 'config.executor.type == native' is therefore false for every config, so a native executor never skips the CLI branch, and branch_on config.executor.type makes if_native unreachable on the research side.

Answered (carried 4 iterations): no normaliser maps executor.kind onto executor.type before the YAML evaluates branch_on. The only adapter is getExecutorKind at executor-audit.ts:204 (kind ?? type ?? native), which runs inside runAuditedExecutorCommand, downstream of both branch selection and token rendering. Its ?? native fallback additionally lets an executor object with neither key self-identify as native in the audit trail instead of raising.

Citation drift: iterations 1-16 cited the auto YAMLs under .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-{research,review}/assets/, which holds only config, dashboard, strategy, prompt-pack template and capability matrix. The YAMLs exist only at .skilled/commands/deep/assets/, so any verify command written against the old path is not reproducible as written.

UX/routing: advisor_recommend for the prompt 'opencode go route this task' returns sk-code first at score 0.783309 (confidence 0.941) and cli-external-orchestration second at 0.316101 (confidence 0.82, ambiguous false) - a routing verb plus a vendor name is answered by the implementation skill at 2.5x the CLI hub, and the CLI hub's compiledRoute resolves the opencode phrase to packet cli-deepseek-harness, i.e. a different vendor's harness.

Improvement: the six hand-written single-executor branch blocks already disagree on the config key for executor identity (type vs kind) and on the generation token spelling (research uses config.lineage.generation while review uses the bare generation token), while their argv arrays agree exactly. Extract buildExecutorArgv(executor,{dir}) and buildDispatchFacts(config) into runtime/lib/deep-loop/ and call them from each YAML the way runAuditedExecutorCommand is already called; without this every future flag or fact must be added in six places and this divergence is the demonstrated symptom.

Extension: a pure-static contract test over every if_* executor branch - extract each {config.executor.*} and config.executor.* from skip_when, branch_on and dispatchFacts, and assert each path exists in the executor schema JSON. Two inputs, one comparison, no dispatch; it would have caught f-iter017-002 at authoring time, and it belongs beside post-dispatch-validate.ts as its pre-dispatch counterpart. A normaliser would instead entrench two spellings; a contract test deletes the second.

UX: with six near-identical branch blocks inside 162KB and 183KB files, a failed dispatch cannot be attributed to a branch from the log - dispatchId is built from the same literal template inside each block so it does not discriminate. Emit branchId alongside dispatchId in the failure event to make the f-iter017-006/007 defects diagnosable in production, not only at authoring time.

Every {config.executor.*} path referenced by an executor branch must exist as a key in the executor schema; otherwise skip_when and branch_on evaluate against undefined and the branch order silently decides.
